statement: A leaking faucet releases one drop of water every $1.5$ seconds, and each drop has a volume of $0.05$ milliliters. At this rate, how many liters of water will the faucet leak in one week? ($1$ liter $= 1{,}000$ milliliters)

choices.misconception: I used the 10,080 minutes in a week instead of the seconds, so I divided minutes by 1.5 and counted far too few drops.
I multiplied the seconds in a week by 1.5 instead of dividing, as if each second produced 1.5 drops.
I found 20,160 milliliters correctly but forgot to divide by 1,000 to change milliliters into liters.

hints: Start by finding the number of seconds in one week.
Divide the seconds by $1.5$ to count drops, multiply by $0.05$ to get milliliters, then convert milliliters to liters.
One week has $7 \cdot 24 \cdot 3{,}600 = 604{,}800$ seconds, which gives $604{,}800 \div 1.5 = 403{,}200$ drops.

solutions.reliable: One week has $7 \times 24 \times 60 \times 60 = 604{,}800$ seconds. One drop every $1.5$ seconds gives $604{,}800 \div 1.5 = 403{,}200$ drops. Each drop is $0.05$ milliliters, so the leak is $403{,}200 \times 0.05 = 20{,}160$ milliliters, which is $20{,}160 \div 1{,}000 = 20.16$ liters.
solutions.elegant: The leak rate is $\frac{0.05}{1.5} = \frac{1}{30}$ milliliter per second. That is $2$ milliliters per minute, $120$ per hour and $2{,}880$ per day, so one week gives $7 \times 2{,}880 = 20{,}160$ milliliters, or $20.16$ liters.
